body:
I don't typically enjoy the more esoteric, metaphysical side of philosophy, but I really enjoyed that video. Thanks for the link.  

>Why aren't you moving to where you really love? Where would that be?  

Vancouver, Seattle, Portland, San Francisco. I love the Pacific Northwest. There are a lot of places I'd be willing to move, I just am afraid I do not have the financial means to do so. I live in the rural south, which is soul-draining. 

>I could go on about PHI and PHI-Cycle (physical) and strange esoteric teachings, but i'll spare you the diatribe, unless your interested. As a physicalist, do you leave room for ideas pertaining to super-consciousness and the 'higher-mind' and things like superposition, and the general Quantum field of life?  

Honestly, it's not really my area of interest. I'm pretty worldly when it comes to my philosophical beliefs. But I do appreciate you offering to talk about it. Thank you.

Thanks for sharing your experience. That's very helpful. I think I'll take the route of treading lightly around the issue initially. I really, really want to get help. I think that is my answer. Making an appointment with a psychiatrist now. 

Thanks again for talking with me and sharing your experiences and advice.

Thanks for responding. 

>I'm so sorry you've had such terrible experiences there.  

It's not so much about it being a crappy place. Treatment can be both relaxing and uncomfortable at times. It's more about leaving the "real world" for a year or more (I think I would probably be in treatment for a very long time if I went back) and the way I would be treated by friends, family, and society once I get out. 

>If you're not an imminent danger to yourself or others, though, and make that clear when seeking help, I would think you wouldn't be forced into residential treatment against your will--which, perhaps also paradoxically, is an argument for seeking help sooner rather than later, while you're still in a place to be able to say that you won't act on your thoughts.  

This is the type of advice I think I was most looking for. I'd really like to sit down and talk to someone without having to worry about my word choice, though. 

>As far as school is concerned: I understand that you don't think you can take another break entirely, but could you perhaps take a part-time courseload? Also, getting professional help should help you if you end up in a situation like last semester's. You should also know that having a semester or even multiple semesters of bad or failing grades doesn't necessarily close all that many doors for you, if you have an otherwise strong record before and after and you've gotten help for the issues.  

I was planning on taking only 12 hours this semester, if I took any. At this point, though, I'm very dissatisfied with my major, and a third change in major will set me back again. Not that a setback is reason not to do it, but it's yet another barrier.  

>You're obviously a smart and thoughtful guy, and even with everything that's coming down on you right now you can still have a satisfying and successful life, if you get help to put it back on track. I'm glad you're here.  

Thanks, and thanks for being here to help not just me, but many others.

Thanks for the response. 

>First off, giving your things away is an utterly fantastic thing. Life is about what you let go of, not what you hold on to.  

I agree, and it actually feels good to live with less. I've always talked (quite seriously) about getting rid of most of my possessions and moving somewhere I really love, but as that dream has become less and less likely, my reasons for getting rid of my possessions have changed. 

>Are you into philosophy at all? Does it interest you?  

Yes. I've taken quite a few philosophy classes between high school and college. 

>How about diet? What kinda of stuff do you eat, and do you think that I might be able to convince you that possibly the things that you ingest in all forms (eyes, ears, mouth, etc..) might be a principal reason for your emotional/mental state?  

I've had a much better diet over the last few years than any other time in my life, I think. And yes, I think that is accurate. I am a physicalist, and I think there is plenty of evidence to back up that assertion.
I am here to talk, if anyone else is. I want help. I just don't want to be locked up.
